title: Zone commitment operational playbook and customer negotiation notes
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures an operator-friendly enforcement playbook for customer-level zone/region commitments (what wecurrently call 'zone commitment'), together with negotiation notes for commercial and solutions teams. It focuses on the operational steps required to validate, apply, audit, and -- if necessary -- relax commitments while preserving SLA guarantees and legal evidence for audits.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to Private and Dedicated customers who require resource-level and data locality guarantees (not the hosted multi-tenant default).
- 'Zone' here can mean cloud region (e.g., us-west2), sovereign zone (e.g., EU-2), or on-prem rack group.
- Customers may request full data residency (compute + storage), compute-only residency, or evidence-of-processing-in-region.
- We assume a supported infrastructure mapping exists (region -> available clusters/pools) and that infra team has pre-tagged nodes with jurisdiction labels (jurisdiction:europe, residency:us-west).

Quick executive summary (TL;DR):
- For commercial negotiations, use a three-tier model: Pilot (soft-commit), Contracted Commitment (hard pin + SLA), Exception-Based (contracted but with documented fallback).
- Operationally, enforce commitments at request-routing layer with two guards: (1) pre-flight mapping check (customer -> allowed zones) and (2) runtime pin enforcement (route + affinity).
- Required audit artifacts: signed routing evidence bundle (per-customer daily), tenant manifest (pinned clusters list), and token-level routing logs for requested window.

Negotiation heuristics for solutions/sales:
- Pricing uplift guidance: +15-30% on top of base dedicated pricing for strict compute+storage residency in a new region; price change should cover capacity reservation, infra tagging, and audit retention costs.
- SLA deltas: Add a 2x latency SLO buffer for region-restricted routes in the contract, and call out fallback policy explicitly (what happens if pinned pools are exhausted).
- Customer concessions: Offer a canary fallback window (e.g., 24–72 hours) during ramp if they accept aggregated audit traces instead of raw logs.
- Recommended contract language snippet (informal): 'Redwood will route and process Customer requests within the Customer-designated Regions where feasible and consistent with the Reservation. If Reserved capacity is temporarily unavailable, Redwood may route to preapproved fallback Regions in accordance with the Fallback Matrix and Customer's exception policy.'

Operational enforcement checklist (day-of checklist for oncall/ops engineer):
1) Verify customer manifest: confirm customer_id has an assigned allowed_zones list and that manifest is signed in the tenant registry.
2) Capacity pre-check: confirm at least 1.2x concurrent capacity reserved in each allowed zone for the agreed profile (model families, sequence lengths).
3) Preflight API toggle: ensure the region_commitment flag exists and is seeded in the routing policy for the customer.
4) Deploy routing policy: push canary routing rule (5% traffic) then 25% then full; watch pin-failure metrics.
5) Telemetry sanity: confirm logging pipeline tags (region_tag, node_jurisdiction, tenant_id) are flowing to audit bucket and retention is set per contract.
6) Evidence bundle: trigger daily evidence bundle generator (S3 path) for customer legal team; validate signature header and checksum.
7) Alert thresholds: create/verify alerts for pin-failure-rate > 1% over 5m, fallback-activation, and audit-bundle-failure.

Technical enforcement design notes (implementation constraints and dev TODOs):
- Routing layer must consult two data sources: tenant manifest (authoritative allowed zones) and live cluster inventory (available capacity + compatibility matrix).
- Fallback policy engine should support ranked fallback lists and time-limited exemptions. Example config shape (pseudocode in infra ticket INF-3472).
- KV cache eviction: ensure KV caches for pinned sessions are stored in-region when commit requires persistent session locality. If fallback used, mark sessions as degraded and record for customer-facing dashboards.
- Model variant compatibility: some quantized/accelerated model binaries may only exist in certain zones; the model-catalog must expose 'compatible_zones' metadata so routing can avoid incompatible fallbacks.

Telemetry and audit outputs required per contract:
- Daily routing evidence bundle: gzipped CSV with columns [timestamp, request_id, tenant_id, model, chosen_zone, reason_code, trace_id] and signed manifest.
- Per-request token-level trace (retained for X days per contract): store in encrypted audit vault and provide an access protocol for legal requests.
- Capacity usage heatmaps: weekly report showing pinned vs. fallback use rate.
- Anomaly signals: sudden migration spikes (>10% go to fallback in 1h), continuous fallbacks for >3 days, or routing mismatches between tenant manifest and routing layer.

Exception and approval flow (for when a request can't be honored):
- Automatic transient fallback (<= 6 hours): allowed if customer preapproved 'short fallback' and marked in contract. Notify customer via automated email + ticket.
- Manual exception (operational approval): SRE/Oncall must open EXC-<cust>-YYYY ticket and get written approval from Solutions Eng + Legal for anything >6 hours.
- Permanent change request: treat as contract amendment (requires Sales + Legal). Document in amendment and refresh tenant manifest.

Rollback criteria and customer communication plan:
- Rollback trigger: pin-failure-rate > 5% sustained for 30m and rollback reduces errors by >30%.
- Communication: triage -> customer success -> send status update with ETA and evidence bundle within 4 hours. Use templated message in shared drive and attach audit snippet.

Packaging audit evidence (operator steps):
- Locate S3 prefix: s3://rw-audit/customer-commits/<tenant_id>/<YYYY-MM-DD>/bundle.gz
- Run validator script (infra/bin/verify-bundle --path <bundle> --pubkey infra/keys/audit-rotate.pub)
- If validation fails, escalate to infra-owner and mark the date in the tenant manifest with "audit_issue:true".

Open questions / items for legal/infra/product: (notes for follow-up)
- Retention windows: what default retention can Finance/Legal accept without bespoke contract? (proposal: 90 days token traces, 540 days routing evidence)
- Evidence format: is CSV + signed manifest sufficient vs. needing cryptographically sealed ledger?
- Cross-border telemetry: can anonymized aggregated traces satisfy EEA regulators in place of raw logs?
- Disaster recovery: how to certify evidence if primary region is unrecoverable? Is DR region automatically a permitted fallback in contracts?

Next steps / action items (owners & rough ETA):
- Infra: expose compatible_zones in model catalog API (owner: Marco Reyes) - ETA 2024-11-21.
- Legal: approve default retention proposal or provide redlines (owner: Linh Nguyen) - ETA 2024-11-15.
- Product: draft contract language + fallback matrix template for sales (owner: Taylor Brooks) - ETA 2024-11-18.
- Ops: build a one-click evidence bundle exporter for CSMs (owner: Priya Shah) - ETA prototype 2024-12-10.

Notes to self / rough heuristics used during negotiation prep (informal):
- If customer request is only audit evidence (they don't require compute residency), push them to 'evidence-only' plan (cheaper, we aggregate telemetry).
- For new regions, always charge set-up fee to cover infra tagging, monitoring, and audit tooling (estimate ~$10k).
- Avoid promising 100% pinning without reserved capacity: ops cannot reasonably guarantee if customer is multi-model heavy and spikes are possible.

History / context:
- Derived from postmortem INF-2781 (Nov 2023) where a lack of preflight checks caused 2 hours of unpinned processing for a financial customer.
- Cross-checked with residency telemetry gaps identified in residency-telemetry-gap-analysis (INF-3330).

Appendix (templates and snippets):
- Templated customer fallback notification subject/body (ops to copy):
  Subject: Redwood residency notification: temporary fallback to approved backup region
  Body: Hi <Customer>, we detected a temporary capacity constraint in your committed region and have rerouted a subset of requests to your preapproved backup region. We are monitoring and will provide a full evidence bundle for the affected window. You will not be charged extra for the fallback per contract clause X.X.

- Sample search query for audit bundle (grep friendly):
  grep -E "tenant_id|chosen_zone|reason_code" /var/log/routing/* | grep <tenant_id> | gzip > /tmp/<tenant_id>-evidence.gz

- Quick links: Confluence spec and infra tickets included above in linked_artifacts.

This is a living working doc. Add notes, copy into a PR for product/legal review, and mark status as 'in_review' once we've locked the retention numbers.
